comments.text_zh: 下面这段视频由 Alan Watts 讲述，Trey Parker 和 Matt Stone 制作动画，精辟地道出了你刚刚想明白的事：[视频] 你本质上是意识到，那些一直被人引导着去相信的东西（事业、财富、社会地位、 possessions/物质占有）并不能让你快乐。如果不小心，这个领悟可能会一路滑向抑郁的暗路，所以要当心，保持头脑清醒。一定要给自己放个假，去追求那些你从前没时间做的兴趣，彻底停止担忧未来。这才是关键的部分——别再想着有什么终极目标是你正在朝它努力的。
comments.text: The following video, narrated by Alan Watts, and animated by Trey Parker and Matt Stone, eloquently describes exactly what you have figured out: [VIDEO] You essentially have come to the realization that the things you have been lead to believe (career, wealth, social status, possessions) are not what will make you happy. This realization can go down a dark path of depression if you're not careful, so be careful and stay level headed. Definitely take time off, pursue interests you never had time for and completely stop worrying about the future. That's the important part, to stop thinking there's some sort of end goal that you're working toward.

comments.text_zh: 我在美国中西部作为基督徒长大，我们一直被教导天堂永存，因此我从未感到任何时间压力。这辈子可以用来塑造品格、在自我提升中挣扎，你可以到下辈子再享受。随着我开始考虑生命结束后就真的结束这种可能性，那种心态对我不再那么说得通了。是的，我想提升自己，因为自我提升和成就会带来更多机会，但我为什么还要拼命追求越来越多机会和成就？是否存在某个神秘终点，到了那里我终于可以放松并快乐？为什么不现在就决定放松并快乐？于是我开始尝试这样做，我觉得正因如此我更享受生活了。我非常喜欢 Alan Watts 这个叫“Life and Music”的视频：[视频]
comments.text: Having grown up as a Christian in the Midwestern US, we were always taught that heaven lasts forever, and therefore I never felt any time pressure. This life can be spent building character and struggling with self improvement and you can enjoy yourself in the next life. As I've come to consider the possibility that life ends when it is over, that mindset no longer makes nearly as much sense to me. Yes I want to improve myself, since self improvement and achievement brings increased opportunities, but why am I striving to find more and more opportunities and achievement? Is there some mystical end point after which I can finally relax and be happy? Why not just decide to relax and be happy now? And so I've tried to do so and I think I'm enjoying life more because of it. I really liked this video by Alan Watts called "Life and Music:" [VIDEO]

comments.text: I would like to share my opinion on living life. What is the main goal? Some may think that it's getting better at something to get a raise and more money. First there is a school, then there is the 1st job, the you try to get a better one and you are trying and trying and trying to get higher. In my opinion, that's not the main point and it's just a side-effect of the life. Article suggests that 1st 15 years of life is a training or a tutorial, but I disagree. They are as much as important as any other time period. Person should do what makes he or she happy. If it's playing video-games or spending time with friends at a bar, it's okay. Of course, it won't affect your skills on getting a better job (so more money), but if it makes you a happier person, do it! Life is all about being happy and doing what you love to do. There is no magic-prize at the end of the life, only memories. What will be the point of having much money and good CV in you will sacrifice your happiness on it. In my opinion, this video[1] nicely shows what I'm talking about. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我想本意是好的，但这看起来更像一篇东一榔头西一棒槌的博文，而不是对“如何选择大学学位”的深思熟虑的回答。最近我听到很多关于“选对大学专业”的说法。为这种事担心很正常，我记得。但我觉得，纠结于选“对”的大学学位是浪费时间。如果你有特别的兴趣，就在大学里追随它们，但别再浪费时间担心自己是不是做了“正确”的选择。我五十多岁了。我听过几百个关于人生曲折起伏、以及大学在其中的作用的故事——包括我自己的。我曾铁了心要当电气工程师，大学头一年半读的都是这个专业。我确信自己注定要发明下一代能源，并借此改变世界。结果我本科拿的是历史学位，（多年后）又拿了城市规划的研究生学位。我在“科技”行业干了三十来年，先是技术文档工程师，然后是可用性工程师，再是软件开发，之后是分析师/产品负责人/随便什么。我认识的最厉害的“工程师”本科学的是美术。他有三项软件专利，还做陶艺。我给那些正面对大学选择的人的老头子建议是：走哪条路没那么重要，迈出步子才重要。就持续行动、持续学习、持续调整，还有，看在上帝的份上，享受你的人生。这是一支舞，不是通往“最终”幸福的长征：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Well-intentioned, I suppose, but this seems more of a scattershot blog post than a thoughtful answer to 'how to choose your college degree'. I've heard a lot recently about 'picking the right college major'. It's normal to worry about such things. I remember. But I think obsessing over picking the 'right' college degree is a waste of time. If you have particular interests, follow them in college, but waste no more time worrying if you've made the 'right' choice. I'm in my 50s. I've heard hundreds of stories of the twists and turns of lives and the role of college in them--including my own. I was dead set on being an electrical engineer, and the first year and a half of college was in that subject. I was certain I was destined to invent the next power source and change the world with it. I ended up with an undergrad in history, and (years later) a graduate degree in urban planning. I've been in the 'tech' business for 30-odd years as a technical writer, then usability engineer, then software developer, then analyst/product owner/whatever. The best 'engineer' I know has an undergrad in fine arts. They own three software patents; they also make pottery. My 'old guy' advice to those staring down college decisions: The road doesn't matter very much. Taking steps matters. Just keep taking action and learning and adjusting and, for god's sake, enjoy your life. It's a dance, not a long march towards 'eventual' happiness: [VIDEO]

comments.text: I completely understand how you feel. You sound successful: academically and career wise. You realise this, yet it's never enough and you compare yourself to the cream of the crop or 'what you could be'. You need to stop this. Constantly wishing for something more while feeling unhappy with where you are 'in the moment' is a bad state of mind. It is not how you want to experience your life and it is certainly not reflective of what you have already achieved. (Many happy people achieve a lot less!) There will always be people that are more intelligent or more successful, and so on. No matter how hard any of us try, there will always be something more to attain and, truly, if you wished to feel superior to your peers then Hacker News would not be the best place to be. Other than at a few elite universities and companies it is difficult to find people as intelligent, refined and ambitious as those found here. (This is not a bad thing! Being around these kinds of people lifts you up.) I am not saying 'give up on trying to attain', and the advice which has been given by many in this thread on how to do so or how to free yourself from tedium is brilliant. But remember that life is not a journey in which the only thing important is moving-up and getting to the 'end'. There is not going to be a top to the ladder you're climbing, and the only 'end' is when you die. comments.why_zh: 以 Alan Watts 的话作为严苛自律的反面解药
comments.quote_zh: 我觉得 Alan Watts 的这段话特别触动人心，或许正是原帖的一剂解药
comments.text_zh: > 这里面很多东西可以被解读为一种让自己避开世界、不面对现实的方式。但任何有用的东西不都能被这样利用吗？有很多关于超越世俗享乐的文本，其中一些非常不错。我尤其喜欢 Ekhart Tolle 的作品，也很享受《Tibetan Book of Living and Dying》……《The Tao of Pooh》和《The Te of Piglet》帮我度过了艰难的青春期。不过，和任何理念一样，把它简化得太过头，往往会丢掉重要的微妙之处。原帖提到的精神上的克己，很可能会引起许多男性的共鸣，他们希望自己有更好的自控力，也希望自己在生活中能有更普遍的主体性。男人对某些男子气概的理想、某些被呈现得很好的原型，完全是毫无抵抗力的。如果这让你感兴趣，我可以强烈推荐 Robert Bly 的《Iron John》、Robert Moore 的《King Warrior Magician Lover》，以及 David Deida 那本出色的《Way of The Superior Man》。我觉得 Alan Watts 的这段话特别触动人心，或许正是原帖的一剂解药：“我们曾把生活类比为一段旅程、一次朝圣，终点有一个严肃的目的，而重点就是抵达那个终点，成功或者随便什么，也许是死后的天堂。但我们一路都错过了重点。它本是一件音乐性的事，音乐演奏时，你本该唱歌或跳舞。”（[视频]）
comments.text: > A lot of this can be interpreted as a way to shun yourself from the world and not face reality. But can't anyone do that with anything helpful? There are lots of texts on rising above worldly pleasures, and some are very good. I'm a particular fan of Ekhart Tolle's work, and I enjoyed the Tibetan Book of Living and Dying... The Tao of Pooh, and the Te of Piglet got me through a difficult adolescence. As with any idea, though, simplifying it too far tends to lose important subtleties. The mental austerity mentioned in the original post is likely to strike a resonant chord with many men who wished they had better self-control, and who wished they were acting with more general agency in their life. Men are complete suckers for certain ideals of manhood, certain archetypes that are well presented. If this is something that interests you, I can strongly recommend the books Iron John by Robert Bly, King Warrior Magician Lover by Robert Moore, and the excellent Way of The Superior Man by David Deida. I find this quote by Alan Watts particularly poignant, and perhaps an antidote to the original post: "We thought of life by analogy with a journey, a pilgrimage, which had a serious purpose at the end and the thing was to get to that end, success or whatever it is, maybe heaven after you’re dead. But we missed the point the whole way along. It was a musical thing and you were supposed to sing or to dance while the music was being played." ( [VIDEO] )

comments.text_zh: > 我们曾把人生类比为一段旅程、一次朝圣，终点有一个严肃的目的，关键就是要抵达那个终点，成功或不管它是什么，也许是死后的天堂。但一路走来，我们都没抓住重点。人生是件音乐般的事，音乐奏响时，你本该唱歌或跳舞。[VIDEO]
comments.text: > We thought of life by analogy with a journey, a pilgrimage, which had a serious purpose at the end, and the thing was to get to that end, success or whatever it is, maybe heaven after you’re dead. But we missed the point the whole way along. It was a musical thing and you were supposed to sing or to dance while the music was being played. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: “生活方式只是描述和/或量化一个人如何生活。”这是正确的。我并不是从这篇文章中得出这个结论，我这样说正是为了直接反驳这篇文章，而我认为这篇文章并不明智。另一个强调我观点的视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: "A lifestyle merely describes and/or quantifies the way one lives." This is correct. I don't draw the conclusion from the post, I make this statement to directly contradict the post, which I believe is unwise. A further video that underlines my point: [VIDEO]

comments.author: Crazyontap
comments.why_zh: 引用这句表达对追梦终归一场空的担忧
comments.quote_zh: 万一我们追逐的那袋梦想，就像这个 Alan Watts 视频里说的那样，其实空空如也呢(1)。
comments.text_zh: 天哪，这条评论对我来说太吓人了。我是说，我跟你素不相识，但“抵达彩虹尽头的那份成功”正是让我每天早上跳下床、每天晚上不想上床的东西。是我的梦想吞没了我，也最让我快乐。但有时我也会想到“它实现之后会怎样”，而事情并不总像我设想的那样。万一我们追逐的那袋梦想，就像这个 Alan Watts 视频里说的那样，其实空空如也呢(1)。你可以说这是否认，但我就是尽量不去多想，因为我不知道未来会怎样，而现在去揣测也毫无意义，毕竟每个人都不一样。不过说实话，读完你的评论我确实有点被吓到了！(1) [VIDEO]
comments.text: Man this comment is scary af for me. I mean I don't know you from adam but getting to the success at the end of the rainbow is what makes me jump out of bed each morning and not want to go to bed each night. It's my dream that consumes me and keeps me happy more than anything else. But I too sometimes feel that "what happens after it's done" and it is not everything I imagine it to be. What if the bag of dreams we're all chasing is just empty like this Alan watts video(1). Call it denial but I just try not to think about it a lot as I don't know what the future holds and it's pointless to speculate right now as every person is different. But reading your comment did scare me a little tbh! (1) [VIDEO]
